title: Claim-state precedence for continuity reconciliation

memory_recovered.statement: Continuity claims must be classified by both evidentiary state and temporal status. A later interpretation does not erase an earlier observation; it supersedes only the operational decision derived from that observation. Unresolved provenance cannot be promoted by repetition, semantic resemblance, or automation completion prose.
durable_rule: observed is reserved for directly inspectable source objects or runtime evidence
inferred is derived from observed evidence and must retain its reasoning and falsification route
proposed is an unadopted candidate rule, design, or interpretation
superseded marks a formerly operative claim or decision replaced by a later evidenced decision without deleting the historical claim
unresolved marks claims whose identity, provenance, or contradiction cannot yet be settled
when two claims conflict, directly observed immutable evidence outranks inference; adopted later decisions may supersede earlier decisions but cannot rewrite earlier observations
automation completion prose is lead-only unless bound to immutable repository or runtime evidence

precedence.conflict_rule: Do not collapse these axes into one score. Preserve all three independently and retain every immutable source locator.

application_to_M_RECONCILE_002.reason: No immutable originating source or exhaustive-history conclusion has yet been recorded for these identifiers.
